headline: UNIDIR warned that cyber threats cross borders within hours, as Gen. Dan Caine named superintelligence a Joint Chiefs strategic priority and NIST issued guidance for transitioning to post-quantum cryptography.

points.text: UNIDIR warned that a single compromised software update can reach thousands of organizations across dozens of countries within hours, and argued no state can address cyber threats alone.
Air Force Gen. Dan Caine, chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, said superintelligence is one of his strategic priorities.
War on the Rocks described how an AI system at Nellis Air Force Base built military courses of action, a complex planning task, far faster than human planners.
The AI Safety Newsletter reported that AI-driven cybersecurity issues are heightening fears of a looming 'Hackpocalypse.'
NIST released a report guiding federal agencies' transition to post-quantum cryptography standards.
A UK watchdog is considering an investigation into the Home Office's use of OpenAI's ChatGPT technology to process asylum claims, citing accuracy and secrecy concerns.
Anthropic's IPO filing led a $235 billion AI dealmaking blitz nearly equal to 1% of US GDP, as commentators questioned whether its post-IPO governance structure can really protect its safety mission.
